speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Health to reduce overcrowding at the accident and emergency (A&E) departments in public hospitals (a) whether the Ministry will implement initiatives to improve health literacy and public understanding of common medical condition and proper emergency care procedures; (b) how is the Ministry raising public awareness about A&E and GP fees, and subsidy programmes like GPFirst; and (c) how is the Ministry planning to incorporate more remote care and triaging at A&E departments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: All these initiatives are ongoing, as we continue to manage rising case loads as a result of frequent outbreak of infectious diseases and an ageing population.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can he elaborate on how urgent care clinics like those in Admiralty and Alexandra Hospital as well as the GPFirst programme, have helped to take the load off A&Es?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will the Ministry plan to introduce more urgent care clinics to reduce the load of A&Es?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, in terms of implementation, will health literacy programmes be targeted towards specific demographics or communities with higher A&E utilisation rates?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Ministry can, then, measure the effectiveness of these initiatives in reducing unnecessary A&E attendances.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The issue has got to do with health literacy and the public education that is received.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As a result, it does not only result in a change in behaviour for health-seeking at an A&E department.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These are public health messages that are useful for the public, in general, to understand about their own health, the health of their loved ones, the health of their family and where and how they can access medical help.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will continue to do so, but I am not sure that I quite agree with the very tight link that the Member has put out in his question.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is worth doing, but perhaps, we measure its effectiveness in a different way.
